title: Brushing and Flossing, Done Right
hook: Brushing twice a day sounds obvious — but for two minutes, with fluoride, and adding daily flossing, is where most people quietly fall short.
key_points: Brush twice a day for two minutes with a fluoride toothpaste.
Clean between your teeth daily — floss reaches what a brush can't.
Angle the brush toward the gumline and use gentle circles, not hard scrubbing.
Don't rinse vigorously right after brushing — leaving a little fluoride behind helps.
content_html: Everyone "knows" to brush their teeth, but the details are where it counts: twice a day, for a full two minutes, with a fluoride toothpaste, plus cleaning between the teeth once a day. Most people manage the brushing but skip the flossing — and that's exactly the gap where trouble starts.
extra_html: The NHS recommends brushing twice a day for about two minutes using fluoride toothpaste, angling the bristles toward the gumline and using gentle, short movements rather than hard scrubbing, which can wear down enamel and gums. Just as important is cleaning between your teeth once a day with floss or an interdental brush — those surfaces make up a big share of each tooth and a brush simply can't reach them. One small but useful tip: after brushing, spit out the excess rather than rinsing heavily, so a little fluoride stays behind to keep working. For technique specific to your mouth, your dentist or hygienist is the best guide.

related.title: Why Oral Health Matters
related.hook: Your mouth isn't sealed off from the rest of you. Gum disease and untreated decay are linked to problems well beyond the teeth — and most of it is preventable.

flashcards.prompt: What does good daily tooth care actually look like?
flashcards.back_html: Brush twice a day for two minutes with a fluoride toothpaste, and clean between your teeth once a day with floss or an interdental brush. Aim the brush at the gumline and use gentle movements.

flashcards.prompt: Why is flossing (or cleaning between teeth) recommended in addition to brushing?

choices.text: It reaches the surfaces between teeth that a brush can't clean
It replaces the need to brush altogether
It whitens teeth faster than toothpaste

flashcards.explanation_html: The NHS advises cleaning between the teeth daily because flossing reaches the surfaces a toothbrush can't get to, where plaque builds up.

flashcards.prompt: What's the NHS tip about rinsing after you brush?

choices.text: Spit out excess but don't rinse heavily, so some fluoride stays behind
Rinse for a full minute with cold water
Always follow brushing with mouthwash immediately

flashcards.explanation_html: The NHS suggests spitting out toothpaste rather than rinsing vigorously, so a thin layer of fluoride keeps protecting your teeth.
